_comment: Values outside safe ranges are rejected and the built-in defaults remain active.

race._comment: Target distance and min/max are used only when a track's laps value is 0.

steering._comment: wind_on/self_center/speed_fade/response_curve shape the virtual analog stick's feel. max_angle_deg/speed_taper are the actual road-wheel steering-lock budget kart_step uses: the full max_angle_deg is available at a dead stop, shrinking as speed climbs (max_angle_deg / (1 + speed * speed_taper)) so tight, slow maneuvering stays sharp while a twitch of the stick at speed can't snap the car sideways.

tires._comment: A compound is a trade, not a rank: grip when warm, against how fast it wears, how well it rolls, and the temperature it wants. Softs win sprints, hards and mediums win long races. ambient_c is the air temperature the rubber cools towards.

weather._comment: CLASSIC only. A patch starts as snow, melts into ice, then into a puddle, and stays a puddle. Soft is the tire to have while it's snow or ice; hard is the tire to have once it's a puddle; medium never wins or loses that trade. puddle_drag_multiplier is standing water dragging at every car regardless of tire choice, on top of that grip trade — it costs top speed, not just cornering. The AI reads the same patches: it slows for one on its way in exactly like a corner it has learned to respect.

turbo._comment: Fully automatic: spool builds on its own while genuinely on the throttle at real revs, along a curve (spool_rate applies at redline; it falls off toward zero low in the band), and bleeds off at decay_rate the instant you lift or brake. A quick gear change just holds it steady rather than wiping it. Whatever is spooled applies straight to engine power as a fraction bonus (max_power_bonus at a full spool), tapered by how much grip is already spent cornering — full effect in a straight line, next to none mid-slide, like a traction control that backs off boost rather than piling more power on top of tires that are already loaded. The 'use' control is a separate, un-tunable instant full-throttle override; see controls.json.

understeer._comment: Pushing past the grip limit costs speed at scrub * (1 + scrub_curve * slip) * dt, so a corner taken barely too hot still just runs a little wide, one taken way too hot really pays for it.

drift._comment: The real dynamic-bicycle-model tire physics: each axle's lateral force rises with its slip angle (the gap between where the tire points and where it's actually moving) up to peak_slip_deg, then falls off over falloff_range more peak-widths toward floor_frac of peak — never all the way to zero, so a sustained slide finds an equilibrium instead of just diverging. weight_transfer_coeff loads the rear under acceleration and the front under braking/engine braking (real lift-off/trail-brake oversteer, no handbrake needed). yaw_inertia_mult scales how quickly yaw rate itself can change for a given turning force. stability_control_strength is the everyday assist that keeps grip driving glued near the tire's actual capability instead of the rear running away with itself; pulling the handbrake takes it out of the loop on purpose, locking the rear to its sliding-friction floor regardless of slip angle — that's how a car spins on purpose now. loose_surface_bonus is the free extra force a yawed tire gets off-road or on snow/ice from the wedge of displaced material it builds, on top of the sliding floor — the reason drifting is only genuinely fast off pavement.

oversteer._comment: A rear-driven car committing hard to a corner on the throttle can rotate faster than grip alone allows, for as long as the driver keeps asking for more than the car can grip (grow_rate_per_second builds it, up to max_bonus). Ease off (catch_decay_per_second) before spin_after_seconds runs out and it settles back down for free; keep pushing and it spins for spin_seconds, rotating at up to spin_yaw_multiplier times the car's own grip-limited yaw rate while losing speed at spin_speed_loss per second.

ai._comment: Lower skill slows the field. Overcommit chance is tested once per sufficiently tight unguarded corner and scaled by driver aggression.

hills._comment: Gravity along a road at angle theta is g*sin(theta) and the load on the tires is m*g*cos(theta). These multiply those two real effects: raise the first to exaggerate every climb and descent, lower the second if you would rather steep ground did not cost grip.

instruments._comment: The simulation has no crankshaft; the tachometer maps how far into the current gear the car is onto this rev range.

camera._comment: Distances in meters, rates per second. Each smoothing value is the fraction of the remaining error still left one second later: smaller is quicker, 0 snaps. corner_lean nudges the aim point toward the signed curvature of an upcoming bend (0 = aim stays on the car's nose); it eases off on its own the more the view has swung round for a reverse.

respawn._comment: Invincibility is visible driving time after the black hold and fade have completed.

wrong_way._comment: Only the human players; the AI's own reverse recovery is never penalized.

tracks._comment: laps 0 means automatic. Width, scale, and elevation values multiply the built-in track.
